questions.q: Why is caching training data especially worthwhile for a multi-epoch training run?
options: Because each epoch reads an entirely different dataset
Because the same shards are read repeatedly across epochs, so paying S3 latency once instead of every epoch is a real saving
Because caching improves model accuracy directly
Because GPUs cannot read from S3 at all
questions.explain: Training passes over the same corpus many times across epochs, so the cost of repeatedly fetching the same bytes from S3 at full latency is avoidable after the first read.

questions.q: How does FSx for Lustre function as a 'cluster-wide' cache?
options: Each node keeps its own separate copy with no sharing
Once any node's read lazily loads a shard from S3 onto FSx, every node on the shared filesystem can read it from FSx at low latency
It caches only metadata, never actual training data
It requires every node to individually re-download the full dataset
questions.explain: Because FSx for Lustre is mounted by every node, a shard pulled from S3 once benefits all 64 nodes afterward, unlike a node-local cache.

questions.q: What distinguishes a node-local NVMe cache from the FSx for Lustre cluster-wide cache?
options: Node-local NVMe is slower than FSx in every case
A node-local cache only benefits the one node it lives on and is lost if that node is replaced
Node-local NVMe cannot store training data at all
There is no difference between the two
questions.explain: Local NVMe is the fastest tier available but has a narrower scope — it helps only the node it's on, unlike the shared, cluster-wide FSx cache.

questions.q: Why does the Solara ML Platform team treat the first epoch of a run as a 'warm-up pass'?
options: Because the model's weights are randomly initialized during epoch one
Because the cache starts empty, so epoch one pays full S3 latency while FSx fills up, making its step times unrepresentative of steady state
Because GPUs need a physical warm-up period before running at full clock speed
Because epoch one always uses a smaller batch size
questions.explain: With a cold cache, the first epoch is slower purely due to cache population — capacity planning should use post-warm-up, steady-state step times instead.

questions.q: What can happen if FSx for Lustre's provisioned capacity is sized smaller than the active training dataset's working set?
options: Training automatically pauses until more capacity is added
The cache can thrash — evicting shards that get re-requested again the very next epoch
S3 becomes permanently inaccessible
Model accuracy improves due to more frequent re-reads
questions.explain: If the cache can't hold the full working set, least-recently-used eviction can remove data that's needed again almost immediately, undermining the benefit of caching.
